messages.content:
The freeze-dryer is not reaching vacuum. Been running 45 minutes and the gauge still shows 4 millibars when target is 0.1 or lower.
Evidence (technician notes): all electrical connections are snug at the pump; pump motor is running and drawing normal current; no visible ice or frost buildup on the coil lines; the intake filter looks clean.

Per the provided evidence: the pump is running with normal current and the intake is clean. The next highest-value measurement is the pump outlet pressure — to confirm if the pump is pulling but the line has a leak or the gauge is faulty. Safety floor: de-energize and release system pressure before cracking any fittings; confirm zero vacuum before contact. Next step: with the system de-pressurized, measure the pump discharge pressure with a separate gauge and record the reading before opening any lines.

Conveyor belt on the infeed is slipping. Only moved a couple feet in the last 10 minutes.
Evidence (technician notes): motor is humming but pulley turns slowly; belt looks dry and cracked; tension feels loose when pressed; no debris in the chute.

Per the provided notes: the belt is visibly worn and the tension feels loose. The next highest-value measurement is actual belt tension with a gauge to see if it dropped below spec. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the motor before adjusting any belt hardware; verify the motor cannot start before applying force. Next step: with the system locked out, measure belt tension at the midpoint between pulleys and record against manufacturer spec before tightening any bolts.

Vibration alarm triggered three times this shift, but when I checked, vibration was normal.
Evidence (technician notes): discharge pressure has crept from 15 psi to 22 psi over the last week; motor windings are warm but not hot; no unusual sounds now; water in the basin looks clear.

Per the provided evidence: pressure is rising steadily while vibration is intermittent. The next highest-value measurement is baseline vibration amplitude when cold-starting to catch the alarm happening and log the exact value. Safety floor: no energized work for vibration measurement, but LOTO the pump if inspecting the suction strainer. Next step: set up a vibration sensor on the motor housing, start a fresh cycle, and record the peak vibration the instant it rises.

Sorter is dropping parcels at the tail end of runs, usually when backlog is heavy.
Evidence (technician notes): all photo-eyes flash green; relay outputs click at correct times; network cable is crimped and seated; main memory shows 80% free.

Per the provided evidence: sensors are seeing packages, outputs are firing, and memory is not saturated. The next highest-value measurement is actual PLC scan cycle time — log full cycles end-to-end with a stopwatch to confirm if the cycle time has crept above spec. Safety floor: no energized work for timing measurements; de-energize before touching any input wiring. Next step: stop the sorter at normal power-down, note the scan time from the PLC status display, then measure cycles manually and record the average scan time.

Wash water is cooler than it should be. Tank reads 115 degrees F but line should supply 140.
Evidence (technician notes): boiler is firing normally; outlet temperature on boiler gauge reads 160; return line is not hot; no steam or water dripping anywhere on the line run.

Per the provided notes: boiler produces hot water at the source and return line is cool. The next highest-value measurement is inlet water temperature at the mixing valve itself — to confirm raw boiler output reaches the valve and the valve is not stuck in return mode. Safety floor: de-energize the boiler and wait for line pressure to drop to zero before cracking any fittings. Next step: with the system depressurized and cooled, measure temperature at the valve inlet and record against the boiler reading to isolate the valve issue.

Cutter is leaving ragged edges on substrate. Quality report flagged 12 pieces last hour.
Evidence (technician notes): blade is not bent or chipped visibly; feed motor turns at normal speed; no grinding or metal-on-metal noise; blade was changed a month ago.

Per the provided evidence: blade looks intact, feed rate is correct, and no mechanical grinding noise. The next highest-value measurement is actual blade depth of cut using a depth gauge on a test cut — to confirm if the blade has dulled (shallower depth than spec) or pressure has dropped. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the cutter before measuring the blade height; verify the blade cannot move before reaching near it. Next step: with the system locked out, make one test cut on scrap, measure the cut depth, and record against the original specification.

Hoist is slow lifting full pallets today, faster last month.
Evidence (technician notes): motor breaker is not tripping; rope looks unworn and sits straight in pulley; load is normal weight like always; power cord is plugged in solid.

Per the provided notes: breaker is not popping, rope is good, and load is standard. The next highest-value measurement is motor current draw under a known load — measure amperage with a clamp meter on the motor lead while lifting a test load to see if current has risen (friction or bearing wear). Safety floor: de-energize the motor circuit before attaching the clamp meter to avoid shock. Next step: with power confirmed off, attach the clamp meter, restore power, run one full lift cycle on the test load, and record the peak current draw.

Scale shows bags as 50 grams heavier than they weigh on the reference scale. Every bag yesterday was reported as 350 grams when reference said 300.
Evidence (technician notes): reference scale reads the same when checked again; load cell is not cracked; no visible spill or product stuck to platform; yesterday's bags were all the same product.

Per the provided evidence: reference scale is consistent, load cell looks intact, and product type did not change. The next highest-value measurement is the scale zero-point reading on an empty platform — to confirm if the scale has developed a positive offset (reads high when empty). Safety floor: no energized work required; simply de-energize for a minute to reset. Next step: clear the scale platform, power it down, restore power, and record the zero reading on the display.

asset: air conditioning compressor in server room

messages.content:
Server room temp has crept up to 78 degrees F even though thermostat is set to 72.
Evidence (technician notes): compressor is running continuously; condenser fan is spinning; no ice buildup on evaporator; return air filter is not clogged.

Per the provided notes: condenser fan is running, no ice or filter blockage. The next highest-value measurement is compressor discharge temperature — measure it with an infrared thermometer on the hot discharge line to see if the compressor is producing cold refrigerant or if discharge temp is high (sign of low charge). Safety floor: no energized work required; use only a non-contact IR thermometer. Next step: measure the discharge line temperature with an IR thermometer and record it, then measure the suction line temperature to calculate the temperature differential.

Freezer is running warm. Brine should exit chiller at 10 degrees F but feels warmer.
Evidence (technician notes): chiller pump is running; compressor clutch is engaged (visible); liquid line has condensation on it; flow sounds normal through the cooler loop.

Per the provided evidence: pump is running, clutch is engaged, and flow is good. The next highest-value measurement is actual brine outlet temperature measured with a thermometer on the outlet port — to confirm it has drifted above setpoint or if the thermostat reading is faulty. Safety floor: de-energize the chiller before touching any refrigerant ports; verify zero pressure before cracking any fitting. Next step: with the system de-energized, place an analog thermometer on the brine outlet, restart, run at normal cycle, and record the actual outlet temperature.

asset: inkjet cartridge system on label printer

messages.content:
Labels have faded ink on the left side only. Print quality is fine on the right.
Evidence (technician notes): cartridge is half full; nozzles look clean under magnifier; paper speed is normal; other cartridge colors look good.

Per the provided notes: cartridge level is adequate, nozzles appear clean, and adjacent colors print well. The next highest-value measurement is pressure reading from the pressure regulator on the left ink circuit — to confirm if pressure has dropped (clogged line) or is normal (nozzles need cleaning). Safety floor: no energized work required; de-energize before opening any ink access panels. Next step: de-energize, locate the left circuit pressure gauge, re-energize, run a test print, and record the pressure reading while printing.

Boxes are drifting left on the belt and jamming against the side guide.
Evidence (technician notes): both rollers spin freely; belt tension is uniform when pressed; no debris under the belt; boxes are all the same size from the same shipper.

Per the provided notes: rollers turn freely, tension is even, and product is consistent. The next highest-value measurement is vertical offset of the belt on the two rollers — place a straightedge across both roller shafts and measure the gap at each end to confirm if rollers have drifted out of parallel. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the belt drive before measuring; verify the belt cannot move. Next step: with the system locked out, place a straightedge across both roller ends, measure the vertical distance at each end, and record both measurements.

Furnace pilot keeps going out. Gas company checked main line and pressure is fine.
Evidence (technician notes): pilot igniter sparks every time; gas flows when I hold a lighter to it; no strange smells; the flue looks open when I look up it.

Per the provided notes: spark is present, gas flows, and flue is open. The next highest-value measurement is actual draft pressure in the flue using a draft gauge at the pilot air intake — to confirm if furnace is drawing proper negative pressure or if stack is blocked higher up. Safety floor: de-energize and turn off gas before inserting any gauge probe; allow adequate time for residual gas to clear. Next step: with gas off and furnace cooled, insert the draft gauge at the pilot air port, restore gas, light the pilot, and record the draft reading.

Emergency stop button works most of the time, but twice last week it didn't cut power.
Evidence (technician notes): button clicks; relay hums behind it; all wiring looks intact; no burn marks on contact pads.

Per the provided notes: button clicks and relay hums, yet power sometimes doesn't cut. The next highest-value measurement is relay contact resistance measured with an ohmmeter during and just after pressing the stop button — to confirm if contacts are pitting (high resistance). Safety floor: de-energize the entire control circuit before attaching an ohmmeter; verify no voltage with a multimeter first. Next step: with power off, connect the ohmmeter across the relay contacts, re-energize, press the stop button, and record the resistance value while held.

Dust collection from the sander is weak. Sawdust piles up on floor instead of being pulled up.
Evidence (technician notes): blower motor runs and sounds normal; discharge hose is clear; a clump sits in flex hose above the sander but nothing blocks it; collection bag is only half full.

Per the provided evidence: motor sounds right, discharge is clear, and bag is not full. The next highest-value measurement is suction pressure at the inlet tap of the collector — measure it with a manometer to confirm if suction has dropped (clogged filter or inlet) or is still strong. Safety floor: de-energize the blower before cracking any access panels or connections. Next step: with power off, connect a manometer to the inlet tap, restore power, run the blower at full speed, and record the inlet vacuum reading.

VFD is throwing a 3-phase imbalance fault and the compressor stops.
Evidence (technician notes): breaker has not tripped; drive display shows all three output phases running; incoming power lines feel cool to touch; compressor is not overheating.

Per the provided notes: breaker is holding, output phases run, and motor is not hot. The next highest-value measurement is line-to-neutral voltage on all three incoming phases with a voltmeter — to confirm if utility supply to the drive has lost balance (one phase is low). Safety floor: de-energize at the main disconnect before attaching a voltmeter; work with one hand in pocket. Next step: with power off, touch the voltmeter probes to each of the three input phases and neutral, then restore power, and record all three line-to-neutral voltages.

Printing press is struggling to maintain ink consistency. Color gets lighter as the run goes on.
Evidence (technician notes): fountain solution is at correct temperature; pH is normal; pump motor is running; no obvious leaks from circulation hoses.

Per the provided notes: solution temp and pH are correct, motor is running, and no obvious leaks. The next highest-value measurement is actual pump flow rate — measure it by collecting outlet flow into a graduated container for a set time to calculate gallons per minute. Safety floor: no energized work required; de-energize if opening the reservoir access port. Next step: place a graduated container under the pump outlet, run the pump at full speed, measure the volume collected over the timed period, calculate the flow rate, and record against the pump nameplate rating.

Thermal images don't match the electrical measurements taken at the same time. Camera showed motor winding at 80 C but thermocouple read 95 C.
Evidence (technician notes): camera battery was full; no dirt on lens; emissivity setting was 0.95 (standard for motor paint); room temp was 22 C.

Per the provided notes: battery was good, lens was clean, and emissivity was standard. The next highest-value measurement is a known reference standard — place a calibrated blackbody radiator at a known temperature in the camera's field of view, take an image, and record what the camera reports. Safety floor: no energized work required; de-energize if the standard is near energized equipment. Next step: set up the reference block at a manufacturer-calibrated temperature, image it, record the camera reading and compare to the true temperature in the reference documentation.

Water hardness is back high even though we regenerated the softener yesterday.
Evidence (technician notes): regeneration ran for 4 hours as programmed; no salt crystals stuck in brine tank; outlet water flows at normal rate; in-tank check valve is not leaking.

Per the provided notes: regeneration ran full cycle, salt is not bridged, flow is normal, and check valve is not leaking. The next highest-value measurement is hardness level of water that has bypassed the softener — turn the valve to straight bypass mode and measure hardness on the outlet water. Safety floor: no energized work required; simply turn the valve to bypass position. Next step: set the valve to bypass-only mode, let water run to clear the lines, test the outlet water hardness with a test strip, and record the reading.

asset: dosing pump on chemical feed line

messages.content:
We are over-feeding chlorine to the cooling tower. Residual is now 3 ppm when target is 1 ppm.
Evidence (technician notes): pump runs at programmed frequency; discharge line has no leaks or kinks; solution in reservoir is clear; pump suction screen is clean.

Per the provided notes: pump frequency is correct, discharge line is open, solution is good, and suction is clean. The next highest-value measurement is actual pump output — collect the discharge for a timed interval into a graduated container, measure the volume, and calculate the dose rate per cycle. Safety floor: de-energize before disconnecting any fittings; wear chemical-resistant gloves. Next step: place a graduated container under the pump outlet, run the pump for a set time period, measure the collected volume, divide to get gallons per minute, and record against nameplate specification.

There is a vibration spike every time the belt goes around the drive pulley.
Evidence (technician notes): belt is not frayed; pulley looks round to my eye; no debris stuck to the rim; bearing temperature is normal; shaft alignment looks straight.

Per the provided notes: belt is intact, bearing temp is normal, and shaft alignment looks good. The next highest-value measurement is actual radial runout of the pulley rim — use a dial indicator pressed against the rim while rotating slowly by hand to measure how much the rim wobbles. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the conveyor motor before using the dial indicator; confirm the belt cannot move. Next step: with the motor locked out, install a dial indicator with the plunger touching the pulley rim at the outer edge, rotate the pulley one full turn slowly, and record the total indicated runout.

Product is exiting the pasteurizer cooler than it should. Target is 140 F but product is 130 F.
Evidence (technician notes): the heater outlet shows higher temperature; circulation pump is running steadily; no steam hissing from any vents; product inlet was the correct temperature.

Per the provided notes: heat source is producing hot water, circulation is steady, and inlet is cold. The next highest-value measurement is temperature at the bypass valve outlet — measure it with a probe to confirm if hot product is mixing with cold bypass flow, indicating the bypass is open. Safety floor: de-energize and cool the system before attaching any temperature probes to metal fittings; use heat-resistant gloves. Next step: with the system running at normal flow, measure the outlet temperature from the bypass valve with a thermocouple probe, record it, then check the bypass valve crack pressure setting in the manual.

The ultrasonic cleaner is not cleaning parts as well as it used to. Leaving parts in longer for same result.
Evidence (technician notes): transducers are not cracked; power switch works; display shows 40 kHz like always; no visible buildup in tank; solution is fresh.

Per the provided notes: transducers look intact, power is on, display shows correct frequency, and solution is fresh. The next highest-value measurement is actual ultrasonic frequency being generated — use a frequency counter to measure the real output frequency from the tank and confirm if it has drifted. Safety floor: no energized work required; de-energize before attaching any test probes; use waterproof equipment. Next step: with the cleaner powered on, use a frequency counter probe to measure the actual ultrasonic frequency from one transducer, record the reading, and compare to the display frequency.

Plastic feed to the screw is inconsistent. Sometimes pellets flow, sometimes they jam.
Evidence (technician notes): hopper barrel is full; feed auger is turning when I check; no visible cracks in hopper walls; moisture indicator on desiccant looks dry.

Per the provided notes: hopper is full, auger is running, walls are intact, and desiccant is dry. The next highest-value measurement is whether the outlet is flowing freely — tilt the hopper slightly or tap it gently and observe if pellets immediately resume flowing (indicates a bridge has formed). Safety floor: de-energize the auger motor before tilting the hopper; verify the auger cannot turn before applying force. Next step: with the motor off, gently tap the side of the hopper outlet while watching for pellet flow — if pellets flow after tapping, a bridge is the issue.

asset: battery bank on uninterruptible power supply

messages.content:
The UPS started beeping and switched to battery mode when the building lost power for 2 minutes, but the system came back normally.
Evidence (technician notes): status display showed all batteries in green before the outage; battery room has no leaks or corrosion smell; terminals look clean; batteries installed 4 years ago.

Per the provided notes: display showed green before the event, terminals are clean, and no corrosion smell. The next highest-value measurement is individual cell voltages — measure each cell in the battery string with a digital voltmeter and record if any cell is lower than nominal per cell specification. Safety floor: de-energize and disconnect the battery negative terminal before measuring; use insulated leads. Next step: with the battery negative lead disconnected, measure each cell voltage with a multimeter, record all readings, and compare to the nominal specification in the battery documentation.

The agitator is making a grinding noise that was not there a week ago. Pitch gets higher as I increase speed.
Evidence (technician notes): motor current draw is normal; no visible runout in shaft; coupling bolts are all tight; lubrication level in bearing housing is full.

Per the provided notes: current is normal, shaft looks straight, bolts are tight, and oil level is full. The next highest-value measurement is bearing temperature — measure it with an infrared thermometer on the bearing housing during a full-speed run to confirm if temperature has risen. Safety floor: de-energize and wait for the shaft to stop rotating before measuring the bearing temperature; use only a non-contact infrared thermometer. Next step: run the agitator at full speed for an extended time to reach steady state, then measure the bearing housing temperature and record it against the last known baseline.

The press does not have as much initial force as it used to. It cycles normally after the first clamp, but the first clamp is sluggish.
Evidence (technician notes): pump delivers flow at normal pressure; valve linkages move freely; no oil leaks in hoses; pressure gauge on accumulator reads normal.

Per the provided notes: pump pressure is normal, valves move freely, no leaks, and gauge reads normal. The next highest-value measurement is actual accumulator nitrogen pressure — shutdown the system, bleed hydraulic pressure, and measure the accumulator precharge. Safety floor: de-energize and vent all hydraulic pressure before touching accumulator ports; verify zero pressure with a gauge. Next step: with the system depressurized, locate the nitrogen charge valve on the accumulator, use a nitrogen gauge to measure the precharge pressure, and record it against the nameplate specification.

Relative humidity will not drop below 55% even though the dehumidifier runs full blast.
Evidence (technician notes): dehumidifier display shows cooling mode; compressor is running; condensation forms on the cold coil; filter is not clogged with dust.

Per the provided notes: compressor is running, coil is condensing, and filter is clear. The next highest-value measurement is actual air temperature entering the cooler coil — measure it at the inlet damper; if inlet is too cold, the coil is freezing and triggering defrost too often. Safety floor: de-energize before working near the coil; verify no airflow is occurring. Next step: with power off, place a thermometer probe at the cooler coil inlet inside the unit, restore power, run for a normal cycle period, and record the inlet air temperature.

asset: label applicator head on packaging line

messages.content:
Labels are peeling off boxes a few seconds after applied. Adhesive seems wet but not sticking.
Evidence (technician notes): applicator motor is running; label roll is feeding; pressure pads look clean; boxes move at normal speed.

Per the provided notes: motor is running, roll is feeding, pads are clean, and speed is normal. The next highest-value measurement is pressure exerted by the applicator head during application — use pressure-sensitive film or measure the gap between head and label pad. Safety floor: de-energize before inserting any measurement device under the pressure pad; verify the motor cannot move. Next step: with power off, place pressure-sensitive film under the applicator head, activate to press once, lift the pad, and inspect the color transfer on the film to confirm pressure distribution.

Generator load-test showed lower power output than the previous test from before. Same load but 5% less kilowatts.
Evidence (technician notes): fuel injection timing has not changed; engine oil is clean; no visible cracks in the block; air intake filter is clean.

Per the provided notes: fuel timing is unchanged, oil is good, block is intact, and intake is clean. The next highest-value measurement is actual exhaust backpressure — install a pressure gauge on the exhaust manifold and measure during a full-load run. Safety floor: de-energize and allow cooling before attaching any backpressure gauge to the exhaust manifold. Next step: with the generator warmed up but off, install a backpressure gauge on a tapped hole in the exhaust manifold, restart under full load, and record the backpressure reading against the manufacturer limit.

The pump is vibrating more than before. Noticed the coupling bolts have some rust on them.
Evidence (technician notes): bolts do not appear loose when I wiggle the shaft; pump bearings spin freely by hand; impeller clearance looks even all around; no knocking sounds.

Per the provided notes: bolts are snug, bearings spin freely, impeller clearance is even, and no knocking. The next highest-value measurement is coupling bolt tension — use a bolt-tension gauge to measure the preload on the fasteners. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the motor before measuring; verify the shaft cannot turn before reaching over. Next step: with the pump locked out, use a bolt-tension gauge on each coupling bolt, record all readings, and compare to the engineering drawing specification to confirm if any bolt has lost preload.

Reverse osmosis water purity has dropped. TDS meter shows 50 ppm when it should be 10 or lower.
Evidence (technician notes): feed water pressure is at setpoint (60 psi); inlet filter has been replaced recently; membrane age is 3 years; storage tank level is normal.

Per the provided notes: feed pressure is correct, inlet filter is fresh, and storage is normal. The next highest-value measurement is actual reject flow rate and pressure differential — measure both permeate and reject flow rates with graduated containers to calculate membrane flux. Safety floor: de-energize and vent system pressure before disconnecting any fittings; verify zero pressure with a gauge. Next step: run the system, collect permeate and reject water separately for a fixed time period, measure both volumes, calculate the flux rate in gallons per minute per square foot, and record against manufacturer specification.

asset: synchronous belt drive on film cutter

messages.content:
Film cutter has started slipping under load. Cuts normally when lightly loaded but skips when material tension is high.
Evidence (technician notes): belt teeth do not look cracked; pulley grooves are not visibly worn; no dust or shavings on the belt; tension feels tight when pressed.

Per the provided notes: teeth look intact, grooves appear good, belt is clean, and tension is firm. The next highest-value measurement is tooth height on both belt and pulley grooves — use a depth gauge to measure and compare against original specification. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the motor before measuring; confirm the motor cannot turn. Next step: with the motor locked out, measure belt tooth height at multiple points with a depth gauge, then measure pulley groove depth at multiple radial positions, and record all measurements against the original part specification.

Motor keeps tripping the overload breaker but when I check, the motor is not hot.
Evidence (technician notes): all three phases supply good voltage to motor terminals; pump outlet pressure is normal; no mechanical locking when I rotate shaft by hand; power cord is firmly seated.

Per the provided notes: supply voltage is good, pressure is normal, and shaft rotates freely. The next highest-value measurement is winding resistance of all three motor phases — measure each phase-to-neutral resistance with an ohmmeter. Safety floor: de-energize at the main disconnect and lock the breaker off before measuring; confirm nobody can restart. Next step: with the motor de-energized and terminals disconnected, measure resistance from each motor terminal to ground and between each pair, record all readings, and compare them to identify any phase with higher resistance indicating winding failure.

asset: pressure relief valve on hydraulic manifold

messages.content:
Hydraulic pressure is creeping up to 4000 psi when the relief valve should crack at 3000 psi.
Evidence (technician notes): pump displacement setting is normal; no leaks visible on any hoses; flow through manifold sounds normal; manifold blockage indicator is green.

Per the provided notes: pump setting is correct, no leaks are visible, and blockage indicator is green. The next highest-value measurement is a second pressure gauge reading taken at the same port to confirm if the drift is real or the gauge is faulty. Safety floor: de-energize and bleed system pressure before disconnecting any gauge lines; use a catch container for spillage. Next step: connect a second calibrated pressure gauge at the relief valve test port in parallel with the existing gauge, restore system pressure, and read both gauges under load to compare readings.

Spectrophotometer readings drift compared to the reference lab. Same sample but we see different absorbance values.
Evidence (technician notes): instrument has been in climate-controlled room for 2 hours; lamp is not flickering; cuvettes are clean and matched; reference blank reads zero.

Per the provided notes: instrument is warmed up, lamp is steady, cuvettes are good, and blank is zero. The next highest-value measurement is instrument wavelength accuracy — run a calibration standard through the instrument and measure at which wavelength the peak response occurs. Safety floor: no energized work required; keep liquids away from electrical connections. Next step: install the wavelength calibration standard in the instrument, run a full spectrum scan, record the wavelength at peak absorbance, and compare to the standard documentation.

asset: expansion tank on closed-loop heating system

messages.content:
Heating system pressure has dropped from normal cold level to half that value, and the pump is cavitating.
Evidence (technician notes): no visible leaks on any piping; purge valve is not weeping; expansion tank looks intact; outdoor temp is cold and heating is running.

Per the provided notes: no leaks are visible, purge valve is dry, tank looks intact, and heating is active. The next highest-value measurement is tank nitrogen pressure — shutdown the system, cool it to ambient, depressurize fully, then measure using a nitrogen gauge. Safety floor: de-energize the circulator and allow the system to cool to room temperature before venting any pressure. Next step: with the system cooled and depressurized, locate the expansion tank charge valve, connect a nitrogen pressure gauge, measure and record the precharge pressure, and compare to the nameplate specification.

The centrifuge is making a bearing noise when running at high RPM.
Evidence (technician notes): outer housing is not hot; the vibration feels vertical not lateral; liquid levels in samples were equal before run; no visible bearing damage when I look at the assembly.

Per the provided notes: housing is cool, vibration is directional, and bearing looks intact. The next highest-value measurement is bearing radial clearance — measure the gap between the rotor and the stator using feeler gauges to confirm if the bearing has worn and clearance has increased. Safety floor: de-energize and wait for the rotor to stop spinning before measuring; lockout the motor. Next step: with the rotor fully stopped and motor locked out, measure the radial gap at four positions around the bearing and record the measurements against the bearing specification.

Grease is not reaching the end of the distribution line anymore. The first two fittings get grease but number three is dry.
Evidence (technician notes): pump motor is running; the intake from the grease reservoir is submerged; no visible kinks in the supply hose; check valve is not weeping grease.

Per the provided notes: motor is running, intake is submerged, hose is clear, and check valve is not leaking. The next highest-value measurement is pump outlet pressure — measure it with a pressure gauge on the pump discharge to confirm if the pump is developing full pressure or if a partial blockage downstream has built back pressure. Safety floor: de-energize before attaching any pressure gauge to the pump discharge line. Next step: with power off, connect a pressure gauge to the pump outlet, restore power, run the pump, and record the outlet pressure reading against the pump nameplate rating.

One idler roller in the conveyor train is loose and wobbles when the belt moves over it.
Evidence (technician notes): the frame it mounts in is not bent; the shaft end play looks normal when I wiggle it; the bearing housing bolts are tight; no grease is leaking from the bearing.

Per the provided notes: frame is straight, shaft end play is normal, bolts are tight, and no leaks. The next highest-value measurement is radial clearance in the bearing — grasp the roller rim and try to rock it side-to-side while measuring the movement with a dial indicator. Safety floor: de-energize the conveyor and lock out the motor before measuring; verify the belt cannot move. Next step: with the belt stopped, mount a dial indicator against the roller rim, measure the radial movement when you rock the roller by hand, and record the play distance against the bearing specification.

The solenoid valve will not open even though the coil is energized and pulling.
Evidence (technician notes): the coil hums when power is applied; the valve plunger moves partially; inlet air pressure is normal; the pilot drain line is not clogged.

Per the provided notes: coil energizes and plunger moves, inlet pressure is good, and drain is clear. The next highest-value measurement is actual pilot pressure at the pilot inlet — measure it with a pressure gauge at the pilot tap to confirm if pilot pressure has dropped below the minimum needed to fully open the main valve. Safety floor: de-energize before attaching any pressure gauge to the pilot line. Next step: with power off, connect a pressure gauge to the pilot inlet tap, restore power and energize the valve, and record the pilot pressure reading against the valve specification.

Pneumatic conveyor is leaking air at the rotary valve. Air hisses when the valve is idle.
Evidence (technician notes): the valve housing is not cracked; the rotor shaft is not bent; bolts holding the cover are tight; no visible wear ridge on the rotor.

Per the provided notes: housing is intact, shaft is straight, bolts are tight, and no visible wear ridge. The next highest-value measurement is rotor-to-housing sealing clearance — measure the gap between the rotor blade and the housing bore using feeler gauges to confirm if the gap has increased from normal clearance. Safety floor: de-energize and allow the system to vent before removing the valve cover; confirm no pressure remains. Next step: with the system vented and the valve cover removed, use feeler gauges to measure the radial gap between the rotor blade and the housing at the sealing point and record the measurement against the valve specification.

asset: blower motor on dust collection system

messages.content:
Blower motor is getting unusually hot during normal operation.
Evidence (technician notes): motor current draw is within normal range; there are no unusual noises; the intake filter is clean; discharge is not blocked.

Per the provided notes: current is normal, no unusual sounds, intake is clear, and discharge is open. The next highest-value measurement is motor frame temperature measured on the outer housing — use an infrared thermometer to measure the case temperature during a normal run and record it against the motor nameplate maximum. Safety floor: no energized work required; use only a non-contact IR thermometer. Next step: let the motor run at normal speed for an extended period, measure the frame temperature with an IR thermometer at multiple points on the motor case, and record the highest reading against the nameplate temperature limit.

The pneumatic cylinder rod is bending when under load. You can see a slight bow when the press is at full pressure.
Evidence (technician notes): the mounting bracket bolts are all tight; the cylinder barrel is not cracked; the rod is not visibly scratched or galled; rod wipers look intact.

Per the provided notes: mounting bolts are tight, barrel is intact, rod surface is clean, and wipers are good. The next highest-value measurement is cylinder bore alignment — measure the offset between the rod centerline at the cap end and the rod centerline at the blind end using a dial indicator to confirm if the bore is slightly bent. Safety floor: de-energize the pneumatic supply and vent the cylinder before measuring; verify no pressure remains. Next step: with the cylinder vented and removed from service, mount a dial indicator on the rod surface near the cap end, rotate the cylinder slowly by hand, record the runout, then repeat at the blind end and compare the two measurements.

asset: check valve in oil return line

messages.content:
Oil is backing up in the return line and not flowing back to the reservoir as fast as it should.
Evidence (technician notes): reservoir inlet is not clogged; the return line hose is not kinked; pressure on the inlet side of the check valve is normal; the valve spring does not look compressed.

Per the provided notes: inlet is clear, hose is straight, inlet pressure is normal, and spring looks good. The next highest-value measurement is check valve cracking pressure — measure the inlet pressure at which the valve begins to allow flow with a pressure gauge connected at the valve inlet. Safety floor: de-energize and depressurize the return line before attaching any pressure gauge to the valve inlet fitting. Next step: with the system depressurized, connect a pressure gauge to the inlet side of the check valve, restore the system to operating pressure while watching the gauge, and record the pressure at which flow starts to return to the reservoir.

The oven will not reach setpoint temperature. Heating element comes on but temperature plateaus short of target.
Evidence (technician notes): heating element glows when powered; the display shows the current temperature reading; the setpoint is set correctly; no visible corrosion on the terminal connections.

Per the provided notes: heating element is working, display reads, setpoint is correct, and connections look clean. The next highest-value measurement is thermocouple output voltage — measure the millivolt signal from the thermocouple directly using a multimeter to confirm if the thermocouple is producing the correct signal for the displayed temperature. Safety floor: de-energize the controller before disconnecting any thermocouple leads; use insulated probes when measuring. Next step: with power off, disconnect the thermocouple at the controller terminals, connect a multimeter set to millivolts across those terminals, restore power, and record the voltage reading against the thermocouple type specification.

asset: float level switch in storage tank

messages.content:
The float level switch is not triggering the pump to start until the level is way too low.
Evidence (technician notes): the float arm moves freely; the pivot bearing is not rusted; the tank walls are not dented inward; the switch contact terminals are not corroded.

Per the provided notes: float moves freely, pivot is good, tank walls are fine, and contacts look clean. The next highest-value measurement is actual switch actuation level — fill the tank gradually, measure the liquid level using a ruler or tape at the moment the switch contacts close, and record that height. Safety floor: no energized work required; simply de-energize before opening any tank access ports. Next step: place a measuring stick or tape inside the tank, manually raise the float slowly, note the exact liquid level at the instant the electrical contacts close or open, and record that measurement against the manufacturer specification.

The differential pressure readout on the filter indicator is not matching the actual pressure drop when I measure manually.
Evidence (technician notes): the sensor mounting bolts are tight; the tubing connections are not kinked; the sensor display shows a reading when power is applied; no visible corrosion on the sensor terminals.

Per the provided notes: mounting is tight, tubing is clear, display is working, and terminals look good. The next highest-value measurement is actual differential pressure across the filter element — connect a portable manometer to the high and low pressure taps of the filter and measure the true pressure differential to compare against the sensor reading. Safety floor: de-energize the sensor if removing any tubing connections; ensure system pressure is normal before measuring. Next step: connect a calibrated portable manometer across the filter high and low pressure taps, let the system run at normal flow, read the manometer, and record the true pressure drop to compare against the sensor display reading.

Limit switch keeps triggering too late. The arm travels past where it should stop before the switch activates.
Evidence (technician notes): the switch mounting bracket is tight; the actuator arm moves freely without binding; the switch plunger extends fully; electrical contacts close when the plunger is pressed by hand.

Per the provided notes: mounting is tight, arm moves freely, plunger extends, and contacts work by hand. The next highest-value measurement is actual trip distance — measure the distance the arm travels from its starting position to the exact point where the switch contacts close using a ruler or dial indicator. Safety floor: de-energize and lockout the equipment before measuring; verify the arm cannot move during measurement. Next step: with the equipment locked out, position a dial indicator or measuring tape to mark the starting arm position, manually move the arm slowly toward the limit switch, measure the distance traveled at the exact instant the electrical contacts close, and record that measurement.

Motor is not accelerating smoothly on startup. It jerks instead of ramping up gradually.
Evidence (technician notes): soft-starter power LED is lit; the ramp-time potentiometer is set to a reasonable value; the motor itself runs normally once at speed; all three phases have equal supply voltage at the starter input.

Per the provided notes: starter is powered, ramp setting is reasonable, motor runs fine at speed, and input supply is balanced. The next highest-value measurement is actual motor output voltage during the startup ramp — measure the voltage across the motor terminals using a multimeter during a startup cycle to confirm if the voltage is ramping smoothly or jumping. Safety floor: de-energize the starter before connecting the multimeter probes; use insulated leads. Next step: with power off, connect a multimeter across the motor terminals, restore power, trigger a startup cycle, and observe how the voltage reading changes from zero to full voltage to confirm if the ramp is smooth or stepping abruptly.

Flow control needle valve will not shut off completely. Liquid still drips out even when the valve is turned all the way closed.
Evidence (technician notes): the valve handle turns freely with no grinding; the bonnet packing nut is not leaking; the inlet pressure is normal; the outlet hose is not restricted.

Per the provided notes: handle turns smoothly, packing is tight, inlet pressure is normal, and outlet is clear. The next highest-value measurement is valve leakage flow rate — collect the drip coming from the outlet into a graduated container for a timed period and measure how many milliliters per minute are leaking past the needle seat. Safety floor: no energized work required; simply allow the valve to vent any residual pressure before measuring. Next step: position a graduated container under the valve outlet, close the valve fully, time the drip for exactly one minute, measure the volume collected, and record the drip rate in milliliters per minute to determine if the valve seat is worn beyond acceptable limits.

Pilot-operated regulator outlet pressure drops significantly when I apply load through the circuit.
Evidence (technician notes): pilot supply line is not kinked; main inlet pressure to the regulator is constant; the regulator poppet does not appear stuck; no visible leaks from the regulator ports.

Per the provided notes: pilot line is clear, inlet pressure is steady, poppet moves freely, and seals look good. The next highest-value measurement is outlet pressure under load — measure the outlet pressure using a gauge connected at the regulator outlet while applying a known load through the circuit to confirm if pressure is dropping due to the regulator control response. Safety floor: de-energize and depressurize the system before connecting any pressure gauge; use a gauge rated for the working pressure. Next step: connect a pressure gauge to the regulator outlet port, apply a full operating load through the circuit, and record the outlet pressure reading under load to compare against the no-load setpoint pressure.
